Rolling down a hill on a skateboard and shooting at an aperture of f1.2 was a challenge. But luckily the @dji_ronin RS4 Mini helps keen everything stable and in frame!

My two tips for nailing this kind of shot:

1. You can half press the record button on the gimbal to lock focus. I did this every time I passed a moving object so my camera didn’t autofocus on the bush. 
2. To activate the tracking module, you can single press the trigger on the front of the gimbal. Instead of using it for the entire shot, I activated it right at the end of the video when the runner was behind me, so I could focus on looking forwards.

One of the most unique ways to see autumn in Kyoto, Japan 🍁🚃

The Eizan Railway Maple Tree Tunnel is a short part of the train ride between Ichihara and Ninose Station, where maple trees line both sides of the tracks.

🍁 Best time to go: Early to late November is usually the best time to see the autumn colors. The dates can change every year, so it’s best to check the foliage forecast before going.

🌙 We went at night: The Maple Tunnel is lit up during autumn, so the view looks so different at night. If you’re visiting Kyoto during autumn, I recommend adding this to your evening plans.

🚃 How to get there: Take the Eizan Railway from Demachiyanagi Station going to Kibuneguchi/Kurama. The Maple Tunnel is between Ichihara and Ninose Station, around 20 minutes into the ride.

🎟️ Tickets: You can buy your ticket at Demachiyanagi Station. 

💡 Tip: Expect crowds during peak autumn and give yourself extra time at the station. For a more relaxed experience, avoid the busiest weekend evenings if possible. 

📸 For videos, sit by the window. The tunnel goes by quickly, so have your camera ready before reaching Ichihara.

It’s a short trip, so it’s perfect for ending your day in Kyoto. Have dinner, take the train, enjoy the maple tunnel, then head back to the city 🍁✨

BASS CANYON: THRU MY EYES 🔊

Every time I come to the Gorge, I feel so incredibly refreshed and inspired to live life. The canyon view is already so jaw-dropping by itself, but when it lays behind the main stage it almost transforms into a painting.

One of my favorite things to do is sit at the top of hill overlooking the crowd and watch closely for all the cute, tiny interactions between everyone. Almost like deep breath, it’s one of the few festivals where I really can take in all the beautiful memories as they come in. 

I’m not quite sure if there’s another place like it in the world. Especially when you combine it with music from some of the best bass artists in the scene and all my amazing friends, it’s really hard for me not to keep coming back.

This video is a reflection of all that stored intimate energy being released into the canyon. Enjoy!

100 personas. 1 dugong. Y yo fui parte del problema 🫣😮‍💨🤯🦭

Viajé hasta Egipto con la ilusión de fotografiar a uno de los animales más increíbles del océano: el dugong, una especie de vaca marina 😁

Pero lo que encontré me dejó completamente decepcionado.

Más de 100 personas rodeándolo, chapaleando, tocándolo, persiguiéndolo e invadiendo constantemente su espacio mientras intentaba alimentarse.

Y yo estaba ahí. Si bien me retiré en cuanto vi esa escena, decidí volver, grabarla y hacer este video 😮‍💨

Había pagado por esa experiencia sin investigar realmente cómo se hacía.

Ese día entendí algo: no todo turismo de naturaleza es turismo responsable.🫪

Antes de reservar una experiencia con animales salvajes, investiguemos quién la opera, cuántas personas lleva y qué protocolos tiene.

Porque querer ver un animal no debe significar molestarlo.

Si quieres conocer el dugong de una manera más responsable, comenta “DUGONG” y te digo con quién hacerlo. 🐋💙

Sony Kando 2026 was one for the books 🇻🇳

I came here thinking I’d leave with a bunch of footage.

Instead, I left with new friends, new perspectives, and a whole lot of inspiration.

Met people I probably would’ve never crossed paths with otherwise, listened to their stories, shared ideas, and was reminded that there’s no one “right” way to create.

Also walked away with so many golden nuggets from @pat_kay and @mikevisuals . A lot of what they shared got me thinking about where I want to take my own art and how I can keep pushing it further. It’s something we’ve always been trying to achieve.

Even just watching creatives from different countries, and of course the Singapore gang gang, work and frame their shots in their own way inspired me more than I expected.

Sometimes you just need a change of scenery and the right people around you to get that creative spark back.

Feeling very grateful to @sonysingapore for this opportunity. 🫶🏻

Его так же называли «Чертов мост», так как ходили слухи о том, что некоторые валуны были привезены Васильевской горы, где находилось языческое капище. 

Так же он засветился в фильме Тимура Бекмамбетова «Ночной Дозор» 🫠

Выбор объективов

Решил больше рассказывать о своем оборудовании:

24-70 2.8 GMaster II - я обожаю вторую версию этого объектива. Он дает очень гибкую картинку, которой затем легко можно придать характер на посте. Так же это самое универсальное фокусное, 95% моих кадров снято на этот объектив

70-200 f4 II - я люблю этот объектив за его размер и наличие макро режима. Он очень легкий и так же почти всегда лежит у меня в рюкзаке, с помощью 200мм легко добиться приятной компрессии

21/32/75мм от Simera-С (дочерняя компания DZO) - очень крутая оптика с диафрагмой 1.5 (дает возможность ночной съемки). Они не имеют автофокуса, но рисунок у них (как и у многих фиксов) - намного интереснее. Хочу докупить еще 50мм, чтобы был еще более комфортный сет.

I sometimes wonder where I would be if I had never found these frozen lakes.

After my accident, for a long time I just wanted my old life back. I wanted to be the person I was before and somehow continue where I had left off.

But these lakes ended up giving me something completely different. A reason to get up ridiculously early, drive for hours, freeze my toes off 😂 and eventually something that felt like a purpose.

My life today probably makes very little sense according to the standards I grew up with. I’m not climbing a corporate ladder anymore. I don’t really know what my life will look like in five years. I spend an unreasonable amount of time checking weather forecasts and looking for frozen water. 😂

But I found joy again. And maybe that’s enough of a reason to choose a completely different path. 🤍
